title: 322. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Vertically Opposite Angles
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the equality property of vertically opposite angles.
questions.question: Which statement is always true for vertically opposite angles formed by two intersecting straight lines?
questions.explanation: When two straight lines intersect, the angles directly opposite each other are called vertically opposite angles. These angles are always equal in measure. Supplementary angles need not be adjacent; their measures add to \(180^\circ\), so the statement that vertically opposite angles are supplementary is not correct in general. Therefore, the correct statement is that they are equal in measure.
questions.hint: Recall the defining property of angles that are directly opposite each other at an intersection.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the measure of a vertically opposite angle given its paired angle.
questions.question: Two straight lines intersect. One of the angles measures \(48^\circ\). What is the measure of the angle vertically opposite to it?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal. Since the given angle measures \(48^\circ\), the angle directly opposite it also measures \(48^\circ\). The value \(42^\circ\) would come from subtracting from \(90^\circ\), which is not the property of vertically opposite angles. Therefore, the correct measure is \(48^\circ\).
questions.hint: Use the fact that vertically opposite angles have equal measures.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the measure of a vertically opposite angle when the given angle is obtuse.
questions.question: Two straight lines intersect. One angle measures \(125^\circ\). What is the measure of its vertically opposite angle?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal. Therefore, the angle vertically opposite to the \(125^\circ\) angle also measures \(125^\circ\). The value \(55^\circ\) is the supplement of \(125^\circ\), not the vertically opposite angle. Thus, the correct measure is \(125^\circ\).
questions.hint: Look for the angle directly opposite the given angle at the intersection.

questions.concept: Vertically Opposite Angle and Adjacent Angle
questions.learningObjective: Use supplementary adjacent angles and vertically opposite angles together.
questions.question: Two straight lines intersect. One angle measures \(110^\circ\). What is the measure of the angle vertically opposite to an angle adjacent to it?
questions.explanation: An angle adjacent to the \(110^\circ\) angle lies on the same straight line, so it is supplementary to \(110^\circ\). Its measure is \(180^\circ - 110^\circ = 70^\circ\). The angle vertically opposite to this adjacent angle is equal to it, so it also measures \(70^\circ\). Therefore, the correct measure is \(70^\circ\).
questions.hint: First find the adjacent angle using a straight angle, then use the equality of vertically opposite angles.

questions.learningObjective: Solve for an unknown in expressions representing vertically opposite angles.
questions.question: Two straight lines intersect. A pair of vertically opposite angles have measures \(3x+10\) and \(4x-30\). What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so \(3x+10 = 4x-30\). Subtracting \(3x\) from both sides gives \(10 = x-30\). Adding \(30\) to both sides gives \(x = 40\). Therefore, the value of \(x\) is \(40\).
questions.hint: Set the two expressions equal because the angles are vertically opposite.

questions.concept: Calculating a Vertically Opposite Angle from Algebra
questions.learningObjective: Determine the measure of vertically opposite angles from algebraic expressions.
questions.question: Two straight lines intersect. The measures of two vertically opposite angles are \(2x+12\) and \(5x-18\). What is the measure of each of these angles?
questions.explanation: Since the angles are vertically opposite, they are equal: \(2x+12 = 5x-18\). Rearranging gives \(30 = 3x\), so \(x = 10\). Substituting into \(2x+12\) gives \(2(10)+12 = 32^\circ\). Therefore, each of these vertically opposite angles measures \(32^\circ\).
questions.hint: Equate the two expressions, solve for \(x\), then substitute back to find the angle measure.

questions.concept: Finding the Other Pair of Angles
questions.learningObjective: Determine the remaining angle measures when one pair of vertically opposite angles is known.
questions.question: Two straight lines intersect. One pair of vertically opposite angles each measure \(70^\circ\). What is the measure of each angle in the other pair?
questions.explanation: If one pair of vertically opposite angles each measure \(70^\circ\), then an angle adjacent to \(70^\circ\) lies on the same straight line and must be supplementary to it. Thus, each adjacent angle is \(180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ\). These adjacent angles form the other pair of vertically opposite angles. Therefore, each angle in the other pair measures \(110^\circ\).
questions.hint: Use the fact that angles on a straight line add to \(180^\circ\).

questions.concept: Reasoning with Vertically Opposite Angle Sums
questions.learningObjective: Infer the measures of the other pair of angles from the sum of one pair of vertically opposite angles.
questions.question: Two straight lines intersect. The sum of one pair of vertically opposite angles is \(140^\circ\). What is the measure of each angle in the other pair?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so if their sum is \(140^\circ\), each angle in that pair measures \(140^\circ \div 2 = 70^\circ\). An angle in the other pair is adjacent to \(70^\circ\) and lies on the same straight line, so it measures \(180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ\). Therefore, each angle in the other pair measures \(110^\circ\).
questions.hint: First divide the given sum by \(2\), then use supplementary adjacent angles.

questions.concept: Ratio of Adjacent Angles at an Intersection
questions.learningObjective: Use a ratio to determine an angle measure formed by intersecting lines.
questions.question: Two straight lines intersect. The measures of two adjacent angles are in the ratio \(1:2\). What is the measure of the smaller angle?
questions.explanation: Let the smaller angle be \(x\). Then the larger adjacent angle is \(2x\). Since adjacent angles on a straight line are supplementary, \(x + 2x = 180^\circ\). Thus, \(3x = 180^\circ\), so \(x = 60^\circ\). Therefore, the smaller angle measures \(60^\circ\).
questions.hint: Represent the two adjacent angles as \(x\) and \(2x\), then use the straight-angle sum.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a multi-step problem involving adjacent and vertically opposite angles.
questions.question: Two straight lines intersect. The measures of two adjacent angles are \(3x+20\) and \(2x-10\). What is the measure of the angle vertically opposite to the smaller of these two adjacent angles?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles on a straight line are supplementary, so \((3x+20) + (2x-10) = 180^\circ\). Combining like terms gives \(5x + 10 = 180^\circ\), so \(5x = 170^\circ\) and \(x = 34\). The two adjacent angles are \(3(34)+20 = 122^\circ\) and \(2(34)-10 = 58^\circ\). The smaller angle is \(58^\circ\). The angle vertically opposite to it is equal to it, so it also measures \(58^\circ\). Therefore, the correct measure is \(58^\circ\).
questions.hint: First use the straight-angle sum to find \(x\), then identify the smaller adjacent angle and use the equality of vertically opposite angles.
